transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-03
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Aquina SRE), Maria Lopez (Product), Jamal Green (Infra)

[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll just run through the latency numbers and then priya will walk through the kernel experiments and streaming tests
[00:18] Sam Ortiz: yep thanks Alex, we got about 45 minutes, same agenda as last week, curious about TTFT improvements you mentioned in the note
[00:29] Priya Rao: cool, I'll kick off. quick recap - we ran the baseline on Reedwood hosted infra with the 7B open model (quant 4-bit) and observed median TTFT around 210ms with cold KV cache, warm around 95ms. those are for seq_len ~128.
[01:02] Maria Lopez: sorry priya, when you say TTFT is the first token from our client perspective? like after the HTTP handshake?
[01:10] Priya Rao: yeah TTFT here is time-to-first-token after request accepted, so excludes TLS handshake but includes routing and kernel startup. on small seqs it's usually dominated by kernel launch and decoding loop.
[01:27] Jamal Green: and those numbers were for streaming on or off?
[01:30] Priya Rao: those were streaming enabled with small chunking (chunk size 16 tokens) but not true continuous low-latency streaming - more like frame streaming. our streaming infra has two modes we tested: continuous stream with progressive token flush, and chunked where we buffer X tokens then flush. chunked had marginally higher TTFT but slightly higher throughput.
[01:58] Alex Chen: quick note - some transcriptions below will have small typos, e.g., "KV cash" showing up.
[02:05] Sam Ortiz: (laughs) we've seen that. ok can you show the table of runs?
[02:10] Priya Rao: sure, I pasted the runs in the shared bench sheet - key runs: run A baseline (hosted, 7B q4, seq128) TTFT 210ms, p95 340ms; run B warm KV cache TTFT 95ms, p95 180ms; run C streaming continuous with kernel-optimized path TTFT 140ms but p95 250ms; run D quant tweaked + kernel selection (cut down attention blocks) TTFT 120ms p95 190ms.
[02:45] Maria Lopez: the p95 you mean end-to-end? that's from our client request to first token?
[02:50] Priya Rao: correct, end-to-end in our benchmark harness. there is some noise from routing but we've tried to control for it.
[02:57] Sam Ortiz: those warm cache numbers look good. curious about sequence length - our prod median is actually about 320 tokens, tail at 1.2k, so the seq128 tests are not fully representative
[03:12] Priya Rao: yeah that matters a lot, we saw TTFT increase roughly proportional to initial seq slice in a few configs. for seq_len 512 baseline TTFT was ~350ms cold, ~150ms warm. seq1024 moved TTFT to 520ms cold. so we should focus on 256/512 for your histogram.
[03:35] Jamal Green: is that due to KV cache population or because longer context increases kernel setup time?
[03:41] Priya Rao: a bit of both. longer prefix means more KV work and also larger memory working set triggers different kernel choices. our runtime switches kernels based on seq_len heuristics and that can add overhead if it falls into a less-optimized path.
[03:58] Alex Chen: Priya, can you explain the kernel choice nuance for them?
[04:02] Priya Rao: sure - simple explanation: we have optimized CUDA kernels tuned for short sequences and others for long sequences; when the runtime detects a long-seq workload it will switch to a kernel that favors throughput, which has higher per-request latency. also attention algorithm variants can change. the transition point in our bench is around 384 tokens for the 7B model on A100s; on other hw it differs.
[04:27] Sam Ortiz: A100s then? our infra is mostly GCP a2-highgpu which is A100-ish, yeah that's fine.
[04:34] Maria Lopez: can Redwood do forced kernel pinning? like force the short-seq kernel even for longer sequences?
[04:40] Priya Rao: you can force kernel selection in config for POC, though you may lose throughput and see memory pressure. we recommended trying pinned short-kernel for critical low-latency paths for first token, and allow fallback for background batch jobs.
[04:56] Jamal Green: what about quantization? you said q4, q5 variants? which are safe for us?
[05:02] Priya Rao: q4 (4-bit) gives best perf and is usually fine for generative tasks; q5 and mixed int8 are more stable for some models. caveat: certain decoder-only models degrade on extreme quantization, so we'll surface quality delta in the bench. we ran an eval on your prompt set, quality delta <2% for q4 on the 7B we used.
[05:24] Sam Ortiz: ok good. any impact of streaming mode on model output quality?
[05:29] Priya Rao: no direct quality impact, streaming is output flushing strategy. chunking can affect perceived latency though, because you artificially buffer. continuous streaming has best perceived TTFT after initial token but it's trickier with batching.
[05:44] Alex Chen: let's talk batching - you're sensitive to latency but also want cost predictability. how much batching did you see in the tests?
[05:52] Priya Rao: baseline we used small batch window ~20ms and max batch size 8; with that we get decent utilization and TTFT didn't blow up. if we increase batch window to 50ms TTFT increases ~30-40ms median but throughput improves 25%.
[06:10] Maria Lopez: does Redwood offer dynamic batching policies by route? we only want batching for non-critical routes
[06:16] Alex Chen: yes you can set route-level policies - low-latency routes get minimal batching, others can use larger windows for cost efficiency. we can demo that in the console.
[06:25] Sam Ortiz: can we see the kernel-level logs or perf counters to understand why the p95 spikes?
[06:30] Priya Rao: you can enable tracing hooks and per-request kernel selection metadata. we can share a sample trace for the runs. that's part of the next deliverable.
[06:39] Jamal Green: great. any surprises in the benchmark that we should know?
[06:43] Priya Rao: one small surprise - on one run the runtime chose a fallback kernel because of peak memory usage, pushing TTFT to ~720ms for a handful of requests. the cause was a combination of longer seq and a concurrent batch job. we've put guardrails to avoid that in production.
[07:01] Alex Chen: Sam, you mentioned your prod tail at 1.2k - are those user-facing flows where first token matters?
[07:08] Sam Ortiz: yes some of them. chat threads in our support console can get long. the API call pattern is also sometimes chained, so first token latency cascades. we need p95 under 400ms ideally.
[07:20] Maria Lopez: p95 <400ms is the goal for user-facing; for background analytics we don't care as much.
[07:25] Priya Rao: ok target net: TTFT p95 <400ms for seq distribution median 320, tail 1.2k with warm KV cache. we'll aim config-wise for short-kernel pinning on interactive endpoints and allow throughput kernels on batch endpoints.
[07:40] Alex Chen: let's discuss streaming specifics - how are you currently streaming? chunked vs continuous?
[07:45] Sam Ortiz: currently chunked with buffer 64 tokens, we see initial payload slow but then steady flow.
[07:51] Priya Rao: chunked at 64 is-ish large; for better TTFT you want smaller initial flush like 8-16 tokens. continuous streaming with token-at-a-time flush is best for perceived latency but increases request overhead.
[08:05] Jamal Green: would continuous streaming increase cost? more rpc overhead?
[08:09] Priya Rao: slight increase in RPC overhead; however the runtime amortizes some cost on the server. also you can use GRPC streaming which is efficient. cost delta usually small compared to throughput and latency benefits.
[08:21] Maria Lopez: curious about fallbacks - in peak load if dedicated pool full can Redwood fall back to hosted or a smaller model?
[08:30] Alex Chen: yes policy-driven fallback - route can be configured to fallback to another compatible model or to hosted tier. that buys availability at cost of some quality.
[08:39] Sam Ortiz: okay good. next, kernel experiments - what did you try?
[08:43] Priya Rao: we tried three kernel variants: short-optimized, long-optimized, and mixed tiling. short-optimized favors small seq compute patterns and lower latency; long-optimized does block matmul optimizations for throughput. mixed tiling attempts to hybridize but was inconsistent. the best TTFT wins came from short-optimized with manual quantization tuning.
[09:06] Alex Chen: can you call out concrete numbers for seq=320?
[09:10] Priya Rao: seq320 baseline TTFT cold ~340ms, warm ~160ms on short-kernel; long-kernel warm was ~210ms. p95 on short-kernel warm ~280ms, long-kernel p95 ~370ms.
[09:28] Maria Lopez: so forcing short-kernel seems like the move for low latency. what's the throughput cost?
[09:33] Priya Rao: throughput dropped ~18% on that model/kernel combo. if your workload is mostly interactive the trade is acceptable. we'll quantify exact RU cost in the pricing note.
[09:44] Sam Ortiz: about privacy and private deploy - we need to see the Private (VPC) option numbers, how much engineering to do on our side, and KMS integration for keys
[09:54] Alex Chen: for Private we provide a customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs. setup time varies; typical on-prem-ish pilot takes 4-6 weeks for dedicated infra and compliance checks. we'll share the deployment runbook.
[10:07] Jamal Green: are there SOC2 artifacts available?
[10:10] Alex Chen: yes we have SOC2 + ISO attestation docs, plus the security questionnaire we can fill out. I'll attach the security pack after the call.
[10:19] Maria Lopez: any blockers on our side to run the 512/1024 experiments? we need trace data and sample traffic, right?
[10:26] Priya Rao: yes please share sequence distribution and some representative payloads (sanitized PII). the bench harness needs prompt templates and average token size. Sam volunteered earlier to provide that.
[10:37] Sam Ortiz: yes I'll export the histogram and a 2k sample set, we'll scrub PII first.
[10:42] Alex Chen: perfect. Priya, let's propose a short experiment plan and timeline?
[10:46] Priya Rao: plan: 1) run streaming continuous vs chunked for seqs 256/512/1024 with cold and warm KV cache; 2) run kernel pin short vs long for seq 320 to get p50/p95; 3) run batching window sensitivity (20/50/100ms); 4) run quant ablation q4 vs q5 for quality check. deliverables: bench spreadsheet + traces + summary. target end date 2027-08-10 for first pass.
[11:15] Maria Lopez: that timeline works for our product team, we'll review results and flag any unacceptable regressions
[11:22] Sam Ortiz: one more question - do you support chunked decoding with server side re-ordering for few-shot prompts?
[11:29] Priya Rao: yes, we support re-ordering and also prompt concatenation optimization to reduce redundant prefix decoding. that helps for few-shot.
[11:38] Jamal Green: any tuning on KV cache eviction we should be aware of?
[11:42] Priya Rao: eviction policy is LRU but we can configure TTLs for route level; for your workload I'd suggest longer TTL on interactive flows to keep warm state.
[11:51] Alex Chen: ok let's recap next steps and owners
[11:55] Alex Chen: Priya will run the bench and share by 8/10, Alex will send pricing and security pack by 8/6, Sam will share traces and hist by 8/9, Jamal will confirm compliance needs by 8/12, schedule private deploy demo week of 8/17.
[12:16] Maria Lopez: sounds good. thanks all.
[12:20] Sam Ortiz: thanks, bye.
[12:22] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, bye.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "Reedwood" vs Redwood). Bench sheet link: (shared) https://redwood.example.com/bench/aquinabank/poc-08-03
